name: Gastric Adenocarcinoma, GIST, Peptic Ulcer Perforation, and Gastric Surgery

reference.source: Sabiston Textbook of Surgery 22nd ed / Japanese Gastric Cancer Association Guidelines
clinicalPearls: Gastric adenocarcinoma classification (Lauren) distinguishes intestinal type (gland-forming, H. pylori-linked) from diffuse type (signet-ring cells, linitis plastica)
Standard oncological resection for curable gastric adenocarcinoma comprises radical total or subtotal gastrectomy with D2 lymphadenectomy
Gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST) arise from interstitial cells of Cajal, express c-KIT (CD117), and respond to tyrosine kinase inhibition (imatinib)
Perforated peptic ulcer presents with sudden severe epigastric peritonitis and free subdiaphragmatic air, treated with Graham patch omentopexy
Early dumping syndrome causes vasomotor and GI symptoms 15-30 minutes post-prandially due to hyperosmolar fluid shifts, treated with dietary modification
reference.pathophysiology: Intestinal-type gastric carcinoma develops through Correa's cascade: chronic gastritis, atrophy, intestinal metaplasia, dysplasia, and invasive adenocarcinoma. Diffuse-type cancer arises from loss of E-cadherin (CDH1 mutation), characterized by discohesive signet-ring cells infiltrating the gastric wall and causing marked desmoplasia (linitis plastica). GISTs are driven by gain-of-function mutations in KIT or PDGFRA. Peptic ulcer perforation occurs when mucosal ulceration erodes full thickness through the muscularis propria into the peritoneal cavity, releasing acidic gastric contents.
additionalDifferentials: Primary gastric adenocarcinoma versus primary gastric diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
Bleeding gastric GIST versus bleeding benign peptic ulcer or leiomyoma
Gastric outlet obstruction from peptic stricture versus antral malignant stenosis
Afferent loop obstruction after Billroth II versus late dumping reactive hypoglycemia
additionalInvestigations: Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy with multiple biopsies (at least 6-8) from the ulcer margin and base
Multidetector contrast-enhanced CT of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis for TNM staging and distant metastases
Diagnostic laparoscopy with peritoneal washings to exclude occult peritoneal carcinomatosis
Immunohistochemical staining for CD117 (c-KIT), DOG-1, and CD34 to confirm gastrointestinal stromal tumor
